title: Singapore Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
meta_description: Singapore Marathon review: 55,000+ runners from 80 countries on 6-7 December 2025, Southeast Asia's only World Athletics Gold Label race, and fast elite times.
dek: Singapore's December marathon drew more than 55,000 runners across two days in 2025, and its elites praised a fast course and good weather. Here is what that edition was like.
verdict: The Singapore Marathon is Southeast Asia's highest-rated road race by World Athletics label. The 2025 edition, over 6 and 7 December, drew more than 55,000 runners, including 14,000 from 80 countries, and it remains Southeast Asia's only World Athletics Gold Label race [1]. The routes pass Marina Bay, Gardens by the Bay and East Coast Park [1]. Uganda's Abel Boniface Sikowo won the elite marathon in 2:15:40 and Ethiopia's Shuko Genemo the women's in 2:41:24, and both praised the fast course and favourable weather [1]. With the half and full marathon on separate days, nearly 850 runners did both [1]. If you want one big-city marathon in Southeast Asia, this is the benchmark.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition
paragraphs: The race weekend ran over 6 and 7 December 2025 and drew more than 55,000 runners, 14,000 of them from 80 countries [1]. Categories were the marathon, half marathon, 10 km and an ekiden relay [1].

The half marathon and full marathon were held on different days, and nearly 850 runners completed the Double Up Challenge, running two categories across the weekend [1]. Singapore's Soh Rui Yong became the race's first double champion, winning the half marathon on Saturday and the national championship marathon on Sunday [1].

sections.heading: The Elite Race
paragraphs: Abel Boniface Sikowo of Uganda retained his men's title in 2:15:40, and Shuko Genemo of Ethiopia won the women's race in 2:41:24, each taking US$50,000 [1]. Both praised the fast course and the favourable weather [1].
The race holds the World Athletics Gold Label, the only one in Southeast Asia [1].

sections.heading: Inclusion and Atmosphere
paragraphs: Canadian para-athlete Chris Koch completed both the half marathon and marathon on a longboard [1]. The organiser, the IRONMAN Group, spoke of runners supporting one another along the route and volunteers creating an encouraging atmosphere [1].
Sport Singapore called it the largest mass-participation run in Singapore [1].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes. It is Singapore's largest mass-participation run, with a Gold Label field, a route past Singapore's landmarks, and the chance to run the half and full on consecutive days.
December in Singapore is warm and humid, even when the elites call it favourable. Pace for the conditions, and book early: the field is huge.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the 2025 edition. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Singapore Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: More than 55,000 runners took part over 6 and 7 December 2025, including 14,000 international participants from 80 countries, across the marathon, half marathon, 10 km and ekiden. It is Singapore's largest mass-participation run.

faqs.question: Who won the Singapore Marathon in 2025?
faqs.answer: Uganda's Abel Boniface Sikowo retained the men's title in 2:15:40 and Ethiopia's Shuko Genemo won the women's in 2:41:24. Singapore's Soh Rui Yong won both the half marathon and the national championship marathon.

faqs.question: Can you run both the half and full marathon in Singapore?
faqs.answer: Yes. In 2025 the half marathon and marathon were on different days, and nearly 850 runners completed the Double Up Challenge by running two categories over the weekend.
